drafts.title: [Connecticut]: Recover native 2024–25 guest assessment and income exports
drafts.body:
Tracks the Connecticut source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

The documented public EdSight SAS exports fail to log on as guest. Complete native 2024–25 school assessment, individual meal-eligibility and enrollment exports have not been acquired.

Acceptance criteria:

- Acquire the complete official 2024–25 school-level exports through a supported public route; preserve native identifiers, raw suppression and file checksums.
- Verify assessed proficiency, valid-score denominator rules, school-year joins and individual PSIS October eligibility; establish grade-school scope separately from SAT.
- Reconcile published percentages and retain unavailable/protected values; keep Connecticut out of the ready catalog until its adapter and model validation pass.

Evidence: [Connecticut 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/connecticut-data.md).

drafts.title: [Kentucky]: Obtain actual assessed school totals or complete valid-score grade weights
drafts.body:
Tracks the Kentucky source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

ASMT publishes grade-specific rates without valid-score counts or schoolwide totals. ACCT grade-band rates can include nonparticipants assigned novice scores. Native economic counts also need a dated source-specific individual eligibility and membership definition.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain actual assessed Math/ELA school totals, or independently verified valid-score weights for every required KSA grade; document regular/alternate scope and nonparticipant treatment.
- Tie the 2024–25 SRC economic count and membership denominator to individual eligibility, including CEP, household forms, timing and carryover handling.
- Join native State School Id/School Code, preserve suppression and audit the intended grade-school population; do not average grade rates with enrollment weights or substitute ACCT totals.

Evidence: [Kentucky 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/kentucky-data.md).

drafts.title: [Nebraska]: Separate actual scored proficiency from nonparticipant accountability assignments
drafts.body:
Tracks the Nebraska source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

Native NEP performance levels can include unexcused nonparticipants assigned the lowest score and differ from participation counts for recently arrived English learners. Coincident count totals and undocumented NotTestedCount=NA do not resolve the population.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain native actual scored-student totals, or a primary complete selection rule excluding every forced nonparticipant and resolving the English-learner achievement/participation adjustment.
- Establish applicable-year missing-code semantics and reconcile independently published numerators, denominators and percentages without interpreting NA as zero.
- Use exact same-year school identities and verified individual ADVISER eligibility only outside CEP; preserve all suppression and update the audit before approving an adapter.

Evidence: [Nebraska 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/nebraska-data.md).

drafts.title: [New Hampshire]: Recover authoritative assessment school IDs and grade scope
drafts.body:
Tracks the New Hampshire source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

The 2024–25 Regular Denominator assessment CSV contains district/school names but no authoritative identifiers. Same-year income now links 483 of 485 school records to the official CCD directory through exact native district/school IDs. This resolves an offered-grade directory crosswalk, but does not identify any assessment row. The public iAchieve entityID export route remains unresolved.

Acceptance criteria:

- Acquire an official assessment export containing native school numbers/entityID, or a published authoritative exact crosswalk linking current assessment records to those identifiers.
- Establish same-year grade-school scope and exact joins to the saved individual eligibility export, preserving academy, charter and interstate population limits.
- Use only exact published schoolwide rates for a point-only model; preserve protected count ranges and omit counts/intervals unless independently verified valid-score counts become available.

Evidence: [New Hampshire 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/new-hampshire-data.md).

drafts.title: [North Dakota]: Establish individual Low Income eligibility or an exact nutrition-school mapping
drafts.body:
Tracks the North Dakota source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

Insights publishes usable exact school outcome endpoints and same-year Low Income rates, but no applicable-year field mapping establishes individual eligibility and CEP/universal-meal treatment. The nutrition alternative uses plant IDs that can span multiple Insights school units.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain a dated primary definition mapping 2024–25 Insights Low Income to individual statuses and documenting CEP, state-paid/universal meals and full-pay treatment.
- If pursuing nutrition instead, obtain an authoritative plant-to-school-unit crosswalk with exhaustive multiple-unit and population rules; exclude every unresolved shared plant and provision/RCCI site.
- Preserve exact outcome bounds, native school IDs and grade scope; use point-only models because no valid-score denominators are published, and never substitute tested-subgroup income ratios.

Evidence: [North Dakota 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/north-dakota-data.md).

drafts.title: [Ohio]: Resolve individual economic codes, reporting-site scope and assessed outcome definitions
drafts.body:
Tracks the Ohio source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

FY25 EMIS permits unverified CEP/Provision blanket economic coding; public aggregates do not isolate individual codes. Nutrition sites can combine schools and do not establish complete annual operating-program or income population scope. The source valid-score business rules also remain unverified.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain a same-year building-level aggregate isolating individual eligible EMIS codes, or establish an authoritative complete operating-program roster and exact reporting-site/school crosswalk for a defensible restricted cohort.
- Document annual income timing, membership scope and eligibility transitions, rather than substituting October nutrition meal-access enrollment or inferring provision status from absence.
- Verify actual assessed Math/ELA aggregate definitions and exact IRN joins; retain null counts/intervals when unverified. The 15 discovered community-school profiles remain unapproved until these gates pass.

Evidence: [Ohio 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/ohio-data.md).

drafts.title: [South Dakota]: Resolve economic eligibility and contradictory invalidated-score rules
drafts.body:
Tracks the South Dakota source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

The accountability economic subgroup includes all students attending CEP/provisional schools. CCD direct-certification definition changes have no exhaustive affected IDs. The 2025 calculation guide and technical manual disagree on whether invalidated scores enter proficiency.

Acceptance criteria:

- Acquire an authoritative same-year individual economic eligibility source, or documented CCD corrections/exclusions identifying all affected school/LEA IDs and their reporting definitions.
- Obtain a native field/population mapping resolving FAY versus All-Assessed proficiency, invalidated/not-scoreable/nonparticipant treatment and the actual valid-score denominator.
- Retain exact historical school IDs and suppression, keep income enrollment distinct from tested counts, and document both resolved definitions before approving models.

Evidence: [South Dakota 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/south-dakota-data.md).

drafts.title: [Utah]: Verify RISE and Aspire proficiency populations and reconcile native fractions
drafts.body:
Tracks the Utah source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

The 2025 rates workbook lacks a source-specific definition resolving actual assessed performance, full-academic-year restrictions and the federal 95% adjustment. RISE published fractions do not reconcile with inspected proficient/tested totals. Repeatable numerical outputs remain audit_pending.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain an applicable-year primary definition tied to the workbook's Percent Proficient columns, or independently published actual scored numerators/denominators for RISE and Aspire separately.
- Resolve the RISE count/fraction discrepancies and every participation/FAY/valid-score adjustment; do not infer school definitions from state count agreement or published band sums.
- Preserve existing exact identity and non-CEP/Provision NSLP exclusions, suppression and assessment separation. Keep audit_pending across rebuilds until documentary and numerical validation establish release eligibility.

Evidence: [Utah 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/utah-data.md).

drafts.title: [Vermont]: Obtain same-year individual school income and verify VTCAP grade weights
drafts.body:
Tracks the Vermont source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

Public Student Characteristics income ends in 2021. Current nutrition percentages use CEP claiming or Provision 2 base-year calculations, while the ISP workbook lacks school IDs. Native 2025 VTCAP grade data also lack an audited valid-score definition for weighting.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain an official 2024–25 school income extract with native IDs, individual eligibility counts/rates, enrollment population and measurement date; an exact authoritative dated ISP crosswalk is a separate possible route.
- Establish actual valid-score denominators for every required offered VTCAP grade, or obtain verified actual schoolwide totals; keep general and alternate assessment standards separate.
- Preserve suppression and audit pure grade-school scope using exact same-year identities; do not backfill 2021 income, use claiming percentages or match records by school names.

Evidence: [Vermont 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/vermont-data.md).

drafts.title: [West Virginia]: Obtain actual scored proficiency beyond participation-adjusted public rates
drafts.body:
Tracks the West Virginia source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

Exact same-year school IDs and individual direct-certification income are available. Native assessment bands show participation-adjusted denominator deficits; separate students-tested fields do not establish actual proficiency numerators, denominators or all population adjustments.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain a primary current definition tied to the public proficiency columns establishing actual valid-score treatment and all FAY/participation adjustments, or native independently published scored-student numerators and denominators.
- Reconcile school percentages and denominators without renormalizing bands, reversing rounded rates into counts or selecting only schools whose bands happen to sum to 100%.
- Retain exact native IDs, the income report's own October denominator, separate grade/high/mixed scopes and assessment populations; publish no ready model until the outcome gate passes.

Evidence: [West Virginia 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/west-virginia-data.md).

drafts.title: [Wyoming]: Obtain authoritative-ID school totals or complete exact valid-score grade records
drafts.body:
Tracks the Wyoming source hold under #2 (all 50 states).

The public 2024–25 assessment workbook downloads successfully but contains school/district names, no authoritative IDs, no schoolwide totals and only protected tested-count ranges. Growth and accountability reports do not supply the missing actual all-tested Math/ELA response.

Acceptance criteria:

- Obtain native actual schoolwide Math/ELA totals with authoritative school IDs and a verified population, or complete exact-ID grade rows with independently visible valid-score weights.
- Establish suppression/capping semantics and actual assessment scope; do not infer counts from ranges/rounded rates, average grade percentages, or substitute growth-only results and accountability categories.
- Audit individual same-year income and grade-school configuration using exact native joins; retain provenance and exclusions before creating an adapter or ready descriptor.

Evidence: [Wyoming 2024–25 source audit](https://github.com/robot-assisted-projects/FRPL-RMA/blob/expansion/all-states/docs/wyoming-data.md).
